exposure: congenital Zika infection at birth (laboratory confirmed)
outcome: adverse neonatal and early infantile outcomes (death, structural brain anomalies or neurologic symptoms)
subspecialty referral for suspected neurodevelopmental delay
cohort: The study included a cohort of 129 children exposed to Zika virus in utero.
finding: Children with laboratory-confirmed congenital Zika infection at birth had a significantly higher risk of adverse neonatal/early infantile outcomes, neurological impairment, neurosensory alterations, motor acquisition delays, and subspecialty referral for suspected neurodevelopmental delay by three years of life compared to those who tested negative.
followup_time: up to three years of life
